solenoid_field.quote: The Mark I magnet produces a solenoidal field, coaxial with the beams, of about 4 kilogauss throughout a field volume of about 20 cubic meters.

summary.plain: The Mark I (SLAC-LBL) detector at SPEAR: a solenoid magnet around the collision point with spark chambers, scintillators and shower counters that tracked and identified the particles from electron-positron collisions.
summary.technical: Mark I: solenoidal field about 4 kilogauss over about 20 cubic metres; 16 concentric cylinders of magnetostrictive wire spark chambers; 48 scintillators (trigger and time of flight); aluminium coil; 24 lead-scintillator shower counters; iron flux return; muon spark chambers.

technology.quote: 16 concentric cylinders of magnetostrictive wire spark chambers that provide tracking information for momentum measurements
technology.value: Solenoidal magnetic spectrometer: 16 cylindrical magnetostrictive-wire spark chambers, scintillator time-of-flight counters, lead-scintillator shower counters and an iron flux return with muon spark chambers
